Only the deployer (owner) can successfully withdraw contract balance via withdrawAll/sendMoney in the reference; the mutant inverts onlyOwner so non-owner callers can withdraw, causing the contract balance (address(c).balance) to decrease for some fuzzed inputs.

Invariant: after any sendMoney call from any caller sending arbitrary calldata/ether to any callee, the contract balance remains equal to the previous balance (i.e., only the owner can cause withdrawals via sendMoney); the mutant inverts onlyOwner so a non-owner caller can trigger withdrawals and thus can reduce address(c).balance for some inputs.

For all callers and calldata, calling sendMoney(...) does not change the contract's balance when invoked by the owner (only the owner is allowed to trigger outgoing transfers via sendMoney in the reference); the mutant that inverts onlyOwner lets a non-owner invoke withdrawals and can make address(c).balance decrease for some inputs.

For every caller and calldata, if a non-owner address (attacker) calls sendMoney targeting a callee that re-enters and invokes withdrawAll, the reference contract prevents the attacker from reducing address(c).balance (onlyOwner blocks them), whereas the mutant inverting onlyOwner allows such non-owner callers to trigger withdrawals and thus can reduce address(c).balance for some fuzzed inputs.

For every caller and calldata, calling sendMoney(...) does not allow the target callee to withdraw from the contract via calling withdrawAll (i.e., address(c).balance does not decrease as a result of sendMoney), whereas the mutant inverting onlyOwner can permit a non-owner caller to trigger withdrawAll on completion of sendMoney and thus decrease address(c).balance for some inputs.

For all callers and values, only the contract owner can cause the contract balance to decrease via withdrawAll (i.e., after any caller calls withdrawAll the contract balance remains unchanged unless the caller is the owner); the mutant removes the onlyOwner guard so some non-owner caller can make the contract pay out to themselves and reduce the contract balance.

For any caller and any starting contract balance, only the owner can reduce C's balance via withdrawAll; the mutant allowing anyone to call withdrawAll can make address(c).balance decrease when invoked by a non-owner.

For any caller and any contract balance, only the owner can successfully withdraw all funds via withdrawAll (calls by non-owners do not change address(c).balance); the mutant removes the onlyOwner restriction allowing a non-owner helper contract to receive funds and thus reduce address(c).balance.

For every caller address, calling withdrawAll never transfers Ether out of C unless the caller is the owner; the mutant removes the onlyOwner check so there exists some non-owner caller (fuzzable) which, when withdrawAll is invoked after C holds a positive balance, decreases address(c).balance.

For every caller and any contract balance, calling withdrawAll does not change address(c).balance unless the caller is the owner; the mutant removes the onlyOwner guard so there exists a non-owner caller (which the fuzzer can pick) that can make withdrawAll decrease address(c).balance.

For any caller who is the owner and any balance in the contract, calling withdrawAll transfers the entire contract balance to msg.sender (the caller); the mutant redirects that payout to owner address value causing the recipient to differ for some inputs.

For any caller who is the owner and for any contract balance, calling withdrawAll results in the caller receiving the contract balance (so address(c).balance becomes 0 and the caller's balance increases) — the mutant instead may send the funds to the stored owner address (encoded as an integer) and thus will not deliver funds to the caller for some inputs.

For any caller who is the contract owner and for any contract balance, calling withdrawAll forwards the contract balance to msg.sender (so address(c).balance becomes 0 and the owner's externally visible balance increases accordingly); the mutant instead calls withdraw(uint160(owner)) which sends funds to the numeric owner value (not the caller) and thus can leave the caller's balance unchanged for some inputs.

For any caller who is the stored owner and for any contract balance, calling withdrawAll forwards the full contract balance to msg.sender (the caller); the mutant instead sends funds to the numeric owner value and can fail to pay the caller.

For any caller who is the contract owner and any payable amount deposited, calling withdrawAll sends the contract's entire balance out of the contract (so address(c).balance == 0 afterwards); the mutant that calls withdraw(uint160(owner)) can fail to reduce the contract balance to 0 for some inputs (it may transfer to an address derived from owner integer or misdirect funds), violating this property.

Reference contract always reverts (fails) when the recipient's fallback reverts during withdraw triggered by owner, because transfer bubbles the revert, whereas the mutated use of call swallows/ignores the revert and therefore can leave the contract balance unchanged while not reverting; the property: owner-invoked withdraw must revert if the recipient contract's fallback reverts when value > 0.

For any nonzero amount sent to the contract, when the owner calls withdraw(amount) the reference contract always transfers out the amount (reducing address(c).balance accordingly); the mutant that uses call may fail to reduce the contract balance for some adversarial recipient behaviour, so there exists inputs (amount and a reverter callee) where address(c).balance remains larger after withdraw.

For any nonzero amount paid into C by the owner and then withdrawn to a recipient contract that consumes all gas (i.e., an expensive fallback that does not revert), the reference using transfer always reduces C's balance by that amount (transfer forwards 2300 gas but still succeeds to EOAs and simple sinks), whereas the mutant using call may fail to forward sufficient gas constraints or behave differently with a gas-consuming recipient causing differing post-withdraw balances.

When the owner calls withdraw(amount) to an address with a fallback that REVERTs, the reference (using transfer) will always revert (so the call fails) for any nonzero amount, whereas the mutant (using call and ignoring the boolean) can succeed (not revert) for some inputs — i.e., the reference always bubbles up reverts from a reverting recipient but the mutant may not.

For every admissible nonzero withdrawal amount and any recipient contract whose fallback consumes more than 2300 gas but does NOT revert, the reference (which uses transfer) will always reduce C's balance by the withdrawn amount (transfer either succeeds to such simple sinks or reverts), while the mutant that replaces transfer with low-level call can fail to forward the same gas semantics and therefore may leave C's balance unchanged for some recipient and amount.

For any call to withdraw(amount) made by the owner when the contract has at least `amount` balance, the reference contract always returns (does not revert) and reduces address(c).balance by exactly amount; the mutant can revert or behave differently when the transfer fails, so the universal property (withdraw never reverts and decreases balance by amount for all admissible inputs) is broken by the mutant for some inputs where the native transfer to the owner would fail.

For any caller who is the contract owner and for any withdrawal amount not exceeding the contract balance, calling withdraw never reverts on the reference contract; the mutant adds a require that can make withdraw revert for some inputs (when transfer would have succeeded but the added require triggers), so the mutant can cause withdraw to revert while the reference never does.

For any owner caller and any withdrawal amount that is within the contract balance and where the owner is a normal payable contract that can receive funds, calling withdraw should succeed (not revert) on the reference C; the mutant's added require can cause withdraw to revert for some adversarial recipient behaviours, breaking this rule.

For any owner address that is a contract which REVERTS when receiving ether, the reference C's withdraw returns (does not revert) while the mutant may revert due to its added require; therefore the reference never reverts on withdraw called by owner even if the owner is a reverting contract, but the mutant can revert for some withdrawal amounts — this test asserts that withdraw does not revert on the reference for all fuzzed amounts when owner is a reverting contract.

For any fuzzed withdrawal amount and any owner address that is a contract which accepts or reverts on ETH reception, the reference C never reverts from withdraw(...) (it always returns) while the mutant can sometimes make withdraw(...) revert; thus the property: withdraw(...) called by the owner always returns (does not revert) on the reference for all admissible inputs.
